https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/1.pr_title: SMS workflow reminder retry count tracking

golden_comments.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Scope the retry-count purge to SMS reminders**

The second `OR` branch (`retryCount > 1`) has no `method` filter. This SMS cron job will therefore delete any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders.

Today only this handler increments `retryCount`, so the impact is latent. But the column is generic and lives on the shared model. Once another scheduler (email, WhatsApp) starts using it, this job will silently delete that scheduler's pending reminders. A purge job should only touch rows it owns.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
where: {
  method: WorkflowMethods.SMS,
  OR: [
    { scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } },
    { retryCount: { gt: 1 } },
  ],
},
~~~

https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/2.pr_title: feat: add calendar cache status and actions (#22532)

golden_comments.comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Webhook-triggered `updateMany` with empty data may not update anything and adds a write to every webhook**

`updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` relies on Prisma's `@updatedAt` being applied even when `data` is empty. That behaviour is not guaranteed. An empty `updateMany` can end up as a no-op, so `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` would never change.

Even if it does work, the value is never read by the UI. The dropdown shows `CalendarCache.updatedAt` through `cacheUpdatedAt`. So this adds an unconditional DB write on every Google webhook or cache refresh for no visible benefit.

It is also unclear from the diff whether `SelectedCalendarRepository` is imported in this file. For delegation credentials, `this.credential.id` may not match the `credentialId` stored on the rows.

Fix: either remove the call, or set the timestamp explicitly so it does not depend on implicit `@updatedAt` behaviour.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, { updatedAt: new Date() });
// or remove the call entirely, since the UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **`deleteCache` throws a generic Error and rejects credentials the UI lets users act on**

A plain `Error` reaches tRPC as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN, and the message is surfaced as a server fault.

There is also a mismatch with the UI. The dropdown shows "Delete cached data" for any Google credential that has a cache, including delegation-credential calendars (`hasCache` ignores `delegationCredentialId`). The handler, however, only accepts credentials where `userId === user.id`. Delegation and team credentials will therefore always fail with an error toast.

The handler also bypasses `CalendarCacheRepository`, even though `deleteManyByCredential` already exists. That breaks the repository pattern the PR adopted elsewhere.

Fix: throw a `TRPCError`, use the repository, and hide the delete action for credentials the user cannot manage.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
import { TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";
...
if (!credential) throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: "Credential not found" });
await new CalendarCacheRepository().deleteManyByCredential(credentialId);
~~~

https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua.pr_title: FEATURE: per-topic unsubscribe option in emails

golden_comments.comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

review_comments.body:
**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Handle missing TopicUser row in unsubscribe**

`TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns `nil` when the user has no `topic_users` row for the topic. That happens when the user gets emails because they watch the category, are mentioned, or are in a group, without ever visiting the topic. In that case `tu.notification_level` raises `NoMethodError` and the unsubscribe link from the email returns a 500 error.

Even when a row exists, `notification_level` can be `nil`. Then `nil > Integer` also raises.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])
current = tu.try(:notification_level) || TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]
new_level = current > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] ?
  TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] : TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted]
TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: new_level)
~~~

**🟧 HIGH** · Security — **State-changing action exposed via GET (CSRF / prefetch toggling)** `unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level on a plain GET request with no token. This causes three problems: - **CSRF:** any third-party page can mute topics for a logged-in victim, e.g. with ``. - **Prefetching:** email clients, link scanners and browser prefetchers will trigger it without the user meaning to. - **Not idempotent:** the action steps the level down on every hit. Watching becomes regular, and a reload (or a second scanner fetch) then mutes the topic.

**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **`unsubscribe_link` translation now requires `unsubscribe_url` for every email with an unsubscribe link**

The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Only the post notification path in `UserNotifications` passes that value.

Other mailers that set `add_unsubscribe_link: true` (digest and other notification types) will not provide it. Examples include the text-body branch of `MessageBuilder` and `html_part`. For those emails, `I18n.t` raises `MissingInterpolationArgument` (Rails default), or a raw `%{unsubscribe_url}` ends up in the email. The spec had to add `unsubscribe_url` just to keep passing, which points to this regression.

I can't see those other callers in the diff, so please check them in the repository.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
# keep the generic string and add the topic sentence only when available
unsubscribe_link = I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)
if @opts[:unsubscribe_url].present?
  unsubscribe_link << "\n\n" << I18n.t('unsubscribe_link_topic', template_args)
end
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Direct `tu.save!` skips MessageBus publish and notification reason**

The action saves the `TopicUser` record directly instead of going through `TopicUser.change`. As a result:
- The `notification_level_change` MessageBus event is never published, so the user's other open tabs show a stale state.
- `notifications_reason_id` and the related bookkeeping are not updated.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: new_level)
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Client-side unsubscribe route never unsubscribes, but says it did**

The Ember route loads data with `PostStream.loadTopicView`, which calls the normal topic JSON endpoint and not `/unsubscribe`. The level only changes on a full HTML page load.

If the user reaches the route through an in-app transition, nothing changes, yet the page still says "You will stop receiving notifications". The message is also inaccurate on a real hit: when the server only moved the user from watching to regular, they may still receive notifications (for example, mentions or replies).

https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua.pr_title: Enhance embed URL handling and validation system

golden_comments.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

review_comments.body: **🟥 CRITICAL** · Security — **Stop rendering imported and edited post HTML without sanitization (stored XSS)** For `raw_html` posts, `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged. Nothing on the import path sanitizes that HTML: - `PollFeed` passes RSS item content straight to `TopicEmbed.import`. - It first runs `CGI.unescapeHTML`. That turns entity-escaped text such as `<script>` into live markup. - `import` also interpolates `url` unescaped into an ``, so a quote in the URL breaks out of the attribute. The resulting HTML is shown verbatim in the forum and in the embed view (`raw post.cooked`). `cook_method` also stays `raw_html` on later revisions. Anyone who can edit such a post (the owner, staff, or wiki editors) can save arbitrary HTML and script through the normal editor. Whoever controls the feed or the remote page, or is allowed to edit these posts, gets XSS on the forum origin. **Proposed fix:** ~~~ruby # post.rb return sanitize_html(raw) if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] # e.g. Sanitize with a strict whitelist # topic_embed.rb link = "#{ERB::Util.html_escape(url)}" # and do not CGI.unescapeHTML feed content; sanitize instead ~~~

**🟧 HIGH** · Security — **Stop calling `Kernel#open` on URLs (command injection / local file read)**

`open(url)` uses `Kernel#open`:
- A string starting with `|` runs a shell command.
- A plain path reads a local file.

`import_remote` is a public method that does not validate its input. The Disqus task calls it with `t[:link]` taken from an imported XML file, so a crafted export can execute commands.

`topic_embed.rb` also never requires `open-uri`. It only works if `poll_feed.rb` happened to load first. Otherwise `open(url)` tries to read a local file and the import fails.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
require 'open-uri'
uri = URI.parse(url)
raise Discourse::InvalidParameters.new(:url) unless %w[http https].include?(uri.scheme)
html = uri.open.read
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Security — **Throttle remote fetches globally; unauthenticated requests can trigger unbounded fetches and feed polls**

The only gate is the `Referer` header, which any client can spoof. Every request for an unknown `embed_url` does two things:
- It enqueues a job.
- That job synchronously runs the full `PollFeed` and then an HTTP fetch.

The throttle is keyed per URL. An attacker who varies the path or query on the allowed host bypasses it entirely and causes unlimited outbound fetches, feed parses and topic creation. Any page on the allowed host becomes a topic.

The loading page also reloads itself every 30 seconds, so each open tab enqueues another job.

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Handle feed items that have no `content`**

RSS 2.0 items usually provide `description`, not `content`. When `content` is missing, `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` on `nil`.

Because of that, the whole poll aborts and later items are never imported. A missing or nil title will also produce invalid topics, since validations are skipped.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
body = i.content || i.description
next if body.blank? || i.title.blank?
content = body.scrub
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Make `TopicEmbed.import` robust to concurrency, deleted posts and caller mutation**

- **Caller mutation:** `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string, and raises on frozen strings.
- **Race on create:** Two concurrent imports of the same URL (the job plus the poller) both see no embed. One of them then raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` on the unique index, after its topic has already been created.
- **Deleted posts:** If the embedded post was deleted, `embed.post` is `nil` and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` crashes.
- **SHA updated on failed revision:** `content_sha1` is updated even when `revise!` returns false.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ruby
contents = contents.dup << "..."
# rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and reload the embed
return nil if post.blank?
embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) if revisor.revise!(...)
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Fix the malformed `end if` in the ERB template**

`<%- end if %>` is not just `end`. Ruby treats the next compiled statement as the condition of a trailing `if`, so the whole if/else block becomes conditional on the buffer append for the following markup. It only works by accident and is fragile.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~erb
<%- end %>
~~~

golden_comments.comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Grafana recording rules lose Pause/Restore/Export/DeletePermanently abilities**

In the ruler-based version, these abilities were gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for all Grafana-managed rules, including recording rules. The new prom-based version gates them on `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`.

The comment says "All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed by definition", but the code uses the alerting-only check. As a result, Grafana-managed recording rules in the new list view can no longer be paused, exported, restored or permanently deleted.

Fix: use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` for these abilities. Keep the alerting-only check for Silence.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~ts
const isGrafanaManagedRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule);
const isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule);
...
[AlertRuleAction.Silence]: [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule],
[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isGrafanaManagedRule, exportAllowed],
[AlertRuleAction.Pause]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.Restore]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, isEditable ?? false],
[AlertRuleAction.DeletePermanently]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isGrafanaManagedRule, (isRemovable && isAdmin()) ?? false],
~~~

https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/pul.pr_title: Implement access token context encoding framework

golden_comments.comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

review_comments.body:
**🟨 MEDIUM** · Maintainability — **New abstract `getShortcut()` breaks existing custom grant type factories at startup**

`getShortcut()` is added with no default implementation. `postInit` calls it unconditionally for every registered `OAuth2GrantType` factory.

Third-party grant factories compiled against the previous SPI will throw `AbstractMethodError` during server startup. The new encoder SPI therefore takes down the whole server, not just token issuance for that grant.

Duplicate shortcuts between extensions also abort startup through the size check.

Provide a safe default, or handle missing or failed shortcuts by mapping that grant to `UNKNOWN` instead of failing.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~java
default String getShortcut() {
    return null; // encoder falls back to "na" for grants without a shortcut
}
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Bug — **Lightweight-token detection in `initToken` relies on context client, risking NPE or wrong type**

`initToken` now runs on every access-token creation path. It calls `getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`, which dereferences `session.getContext().getClient()`.

Before this change the helper was only called from protocol mappers. Some token-creation paths may have no client set on the context, or may have a client that differs from the token's client. This risk depends on callers outside the diff (for example admin token evaluation, token exchange, or internal token generation). Two failure modes follow:
- **Null context client:** token creation now fails with an NPE.
- **Different context client:** the encoded token type reflects the wrong client.

Use the client from the `ClientSessionContext` (`clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient()`) and null-guard it.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~java
ClientModel client = clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient();
Object attr = session.getAttribute(Constants.USE_LIGHTWEIGHT_ACCESS_TOKEN_ENABLED);
boolean useLightweightToken = (client != null && Boolean.parseBoolean(client.getAttribute(Constants.USE_LIGHTWEIGHT_ACCESS_TOKEN_ENABLED)))
        || Boolean.TRUE.equals(attr);
~~~

golden_comments.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua.az_comment: reviewed commit is not in the repo

golden_comments.comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.
to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.

review_comments.body:
**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Use `default_factory` for `queued`; the current default is fixed at import time**

`queued: datetime = timezone.now()` runs once, when the class is defined at module import. Every `AssignmentSource` created afterwards (for example via `from_integration`) gets the same timestamp: the process start time, not the time the assignment was queued.

The field looks meaningful but is silently wrong. Any later logic that relies on it (ordering, staleness checks, debouncing sync loops) will misbehave. The tests miss this because they only check that `queued is not None`.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~python
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AssignmentSource:
    source_name: str
    integration_id: int
    queued: datetime = field(default_factory=timezone.now)
~~~

**🟨 MEDIUM** · Implementation — **Add `assignment_source` to `sync_assignee_outbound`, not `sync_status_outbound`**

The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`. However, the abstract signature that was changed is `sync_status_outbound`, which this PR never calls with that argument.

The `sync_assignee_outbound` abstract contract does not declare the new kwarg. Any concrete integration whose `sync_assignee_outbound` lacks `**kwargs` will raise `TypeError` at task runtime, and assignee sync for that provider will break.

I can't verify every implementation from this diff, so I've rated this MEDIUM. Fix:
- Revert the `sync_status_outbound` signature change.
- Add the parameter to the `sync_assignee_outbound` abstract method.
- Make sure all implementations accept it.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~python
@abstractmethod
def sync_assignee_outbound(
    self,
    external_issue,
    user,
    assign=True,
    assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None,
    **kwargs,
):
    ...
~~~

https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull.pr_title: feat(workflow_engine): Add in hook for producing occurrences from the stateful detector

golden_comments.comment: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.

Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.

review_comments.body:
**🟧 HIGH** · Bug — **Make `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` concrete before using it as a handler**

`MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` has abstract methods: `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. That makes `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` an abstract class.

`Detector.detector_handler` instantiates `group_type.detector_handler(self)`. For any detector whose type is the metric alert group type, that call will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. The exception escapes `process_detectors` and aborts processing of every detector in the batch.

Before this change, the class was a safe no-op that returned `[]`.

Fix options:
- Keep a concrete stub until the real implementation exists, or
- Implement the three abstract methods with safe no-op defaults.

**Proposed fix:**

~~~python
class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):
    def get_dedupe_value(self, data_packet: DataPacket[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]) -> int:
        return 0  # TODO

    def get_group_key_values(
        self, data_packet: DataPacket[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]
    ) -> dict[DetectorGroupKey, int]:
        return {}  # TODO

    def build_occurrence_and_event_data(
        self, group_key: DetectorGroupKey, value: int, new_status: PriorityLevel
    ) -> tuple[IssueOccurrence, dict[str, Any]]:
        raise NotImplementedError
~~~
